description: Add a Dapper-like RediSearch read API on top of RedisQuery so command-oriented .NET teams can execute parameterized queries and materialize typed results without using IQueryable.

userStories.title: Add public search query entry point
userStories.description: As a .NET developer who prefers explicit commands, I want a public async API entry point for RediSearch queries so that I can execute reads without constructing IQueryable instances.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a public async query API for RediSearch reads without requiring IQueryable
The API accepts an index name or equivalent index-targeting input
Add XML docs or markdown example showing basic query-string execution
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Route the new API through RedisQuery internals
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the command-oriented API to reuse RedisQuery internals so that RediSearch execution behavior does not diverge.
acceptanceCriteria: The new query entry point uses RedisQuery or shared internal query infrastructure instead of a separate execution path
Equivalent read scenarios use the same underlying execution behavior as existing query APIs
Add or update a test proving the new API does not bypass shared query internals
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Add named parameter binding for search queries
userStories.description: As a .NET developer, I want to bind named parameters into RediSearch queries so that I do not have to manually concatenate values into query strings.
acceptanceCriteria: The API accepts a parameter object, dictionary, or equivalent named-parameter input
Named parameters are bound into RediSearch query execution for supported query scenarios
Missing or invalid required parameters produce a deterministic error
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Support full document materialization
userStories.description: As a .NET developer, I want query results to materialize into mapped Redis OM document types so that I can reuse existing model definitions.
acceptanceCriteria: Search query results can be materialized into registered Redis OM document types
Materialization reuses existing serialization and property mapping rules where applicable
Null or missing fields are handled consistently with current Redis OM materialization behavior
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Add field selection for projection scenarios
userStories.description: As a .NET developer, I want to specify returned fields so that projection queries can fetch only the data needed for a result type.
acceptanceCriteria: The API supports selecting a subset of returned fields for projection scenarios
Selected fields are passed through to RediSearch execution without forcing full-document hydration
Add documentation or example usage for field selection
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Materialize projections into typed DTOs
userStories.description: As a .NET developer, I want to map selected fields into custom DTO types so that query results can match application-specific read models.
acceptanceCriteria: Returned field subsets can be materialized into a custom DTO type
Projection mapping uses a documented and deterministic field-to-property rule
Projection queries do not require unrelated document fields to be present
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Define anonymous-like projection result shape
userStories.description: As a .NET developer, I want a lightweight ad hoc projection result shape so that simple reads do not require a dedicated DTO for every query.
acceptanceCriteria: Implement one documented anonymous-like projection approach such as a dynamic row object or equivalent helper type
The public API does not depend on constructing C# anonymous types across public boundaries
Document the limitations and intended usage of the selected result shape
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Add aggregation execution entry point
userStories.description: As a .NET developer, I want the same command-oriented surface to execute RediSearch aggregations so that searches and aggregations share a consistent programming model.
acceptanceCriteria: Add an aggregation execution path to the interoperability layer
Aggregation execution is documented separately from standard search-result execution where behavior differs
Add at least one example showing aggregation usage from the new API
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Map aggregation rows into typed results
userStories.description: As a .NET developer, I want aggregation rows to map into typed result models so that aggregation queries can feed application DTOs directly.
acceptanceCriteria: Aggregation results can be materialized into a typed result model or documented row object
The API clearly distinguishes aggregation-result mapping from full-document materialization
Add automated coverage for typed aggregation result mapping
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Document command-oriented API scope and GitHub workflow
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want clear documentation for the new API's supported scope and contribution workflow so that teams use it correctly and repository automation targets the intended fork.
acceptanceCriteria: Documentation states that the feature is a command-oriented RediSearch layer and not a general-purpose low-level Redis client
Documentation includes examples for search queries, named parameters, full-document mapping, DTO projection, anonymous-like projections, and aggregation
Documentation states that any GitHub issue, PR, or automation interaction for this work must target https://github.com/slorello89/redis-om-dotnet
Typecheck passes
